content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the affected plant part and key visual features.

The test image shows a banana plant with: browning/darkening of the outer pseudostem sheaths, dried/dead leaf sheaths at the base, and the characteristic progressive die-back from outside in while the center remains green. This strongly suggests a stem/whole-plant disease. Let me check the part index.

The affected parts are stem and whole_plant. Among the available classes, candidates are: **Panama_Disease** (stem), **Anthracnose** (stem, whole_plant), **Bunchy_Top** (whole_plant), and **Cigar_End_Rot** (stem). I'll view one reference from each top candidate first, starting with Panama_Disease stem.
Panama Disease stem reference shows internal cross-section yellowing. Let me check the leaf references for Panama Disease and then Bunchy_Top.
Panama Disease leaf reference shows characteristic yellowing with dark streaks - matches the progressive die-back pattern. Now let me check Bunchy_Top.
Bunchy_Top shows compact rosette growth - very different from the test image. Now let me check Anthracnose whole_plant.
Anthracnose affects fruit/pods, not matching the test image's whole-plant stem browning. Let me view more Panama Disease references and check Cigar_End_Rot.
Panama Disease leaf reference confirms the yellow-to-brown progressive die-back. Now let me check Cigar_End_Rot and then the remaining classes.
Cigar_End_Rot affects fruit tips - not matching. Let me view the remaining two classes to complete one view per class.

Cordana Leaf Spot has discrete circular spots; Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka has yellow/black streaks. Neither matches. I've completed one view per class - Panama_Disease is the clear frontrunner. I have 9 views remaining. Let me view more Panama_Disease and compare remaining Bunchy_Top references.

Bunchy Top leaf reference is a presentation slide with little diagnostic value. My confidence in Panama_Disease is strong. Let me use remaining views to check more Sigatoka and Cordana references, then confirm with additional Panama_Disease views.
Both confirm non-matching patterns for Sigatoka and Cordana. Let me use remaining 5 views to cover the rest of the references.
Both confirm non-matching patterns. Let me view the final 3 references.

I've now used all 16 reference views. Here is my complete analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Whole banana plant in a group
- Heavily darkened/black-brown outer pseudostem sheaths (especially on the right)
- Dead, dried leaf sheaths at the base
- Center/inner leaves still green and growing
- Progressive die-back from outer layers inward

**Class comparison:**
| Class | Match |
|---|---|
| Panama_Disease | **Strong match** — leaf refs show outer yellowing/browning while center stays green; stem ref shows internal discoloration |
| Bunchy_Top | No match — compact rosette with short, narrow upright leaves |
| Anthracnose | No match — affects fruit pods with dark lesions |
| Cigar_End_Rot | No match — affects fruit tip ends |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | No match — discrete oval spots on leaf lamina |
| Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka | No match — yellow/black streaking patterns on leaves |

The test image is a textbook presentation of **Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt)**: the progressive browning and death of outer pseudostem sheaths while the inner growing point remains green, with dead skirt of dried leaf bases — all classic hallmarks of this soil-borne fungal wilt.
